//exclude: `include` is `**/*.ts`, so anything a build drops inside the repo becomes
the typechecker's problem. Xcode's SPM checkouts are the live example:
point -derivedDataPath at ios/DerivedData (which .gitignore already
expects) and SourcePackages/checkouts fills with third-party TypeScript —
purchases-hybrid-common ships its own Jest suite — and `npx tsc --noEmit`
starts reporting 'Cannot find name expect' in a vendored file nobody in
this project wrote. Build output is not source; list it here.
marketing/ is the same problem from the other direction: it is real
source, but each subdirectory is a separate Remotion project with its own
package.json, its own React types and its own tsconfig. Typechecking them
from here fails on imports this project has never installed. They are
checked by their own `npm run lint`, from inside their own directories.
THE WHOLE DIRECTORY, not one child. This entry said marketing/video and
that shipped a failing Vercel build: there are two Remotion projects,
marketing/video and marketing/tiktok-video, and the one that was failing
was the one not named. A path pattern matches a prefix, not a sibling.
Excluding the parent means the next Remotion project added under here is
covered on the day it lands rather than the day it breaks a deploy.
AND IT CANNOT BE CHECKED FROM A DEVELOPER MACHINE, which is why the narrow
version looked right. marketing/tiktok-video has its own node_modules from
somebody running npm install inside it, so tsc resolves @remotion/cli here
and reports nothing. The root package-lock.json carries zero @remotion
entries and Vercel installs only that, so the imports resolve locally and
fail in CI. Reproducing it needs a clean checkout with a root-only install,
not a tsc run in this working tree.
